seats: a secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.why: Job 41:24 in the Berean is 'His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone': Leviathan's body, not a hardened heart; it shows neither the label nor the sense. 2 Cor 3:15 is 'a veil covers their hearts', which is not hardening (3:14 says the minds were hardened, a different verse).
fixes.fix: Move Job 41:24 to 'The body: pierced, struck, over the heart' (or drop it if the Berean's 'chest' is judged not to show the word). Move 2 Cor 3:15 to the row on the heart that does not understand, or keep it with a note that it says 'a veil covers their hearts'.

fixes.row: In believers' hearts: the Spirit, Christ, the peace of God; cleansed by faith
fixes.why: The label says each verse names the Spirit, Christ, God or the peace of God with believers' hearts. 1 John 3:19-21 names none of these in that way: 3:20 is 'Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things'. The row's own note admits it is about something else. Eph 5:19 ('sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord') and Col 2:2 (hearts encouraged, united in love) do not fit the label either. The 1 John verses belong where the text puts them: God knowing the heart, and the heart that condemns.
fixes.fix: Take 1 John 3:19-21 out of this row. Put 3:20 in 'The LORD, God, searches, tests and knows the heart' (God greater than the heart, who knows all things) and 3:19-21 in the troubled/comforted row (the heart that condemns). Drop Eph 5:19 and Col 2:2 from this row (both already sit in rows 12 and 14). Delete the 1 John sentence from this row's note.

fixes.row: Says, thinks, plans, reasons and ponders in the heart; takes it to heart, considers
fixes.why: The note ends 'It is the heart as the mind and the will, not as feeling.' That contradicts the hub itself, which has whole rows on the glad heart, the broken and afraid heart, and desire. It also lays English faculty-psychology (mind, will, feeling) over the Hebrew lev, which the text does not divide that way. The same assertion appears as 'The heart here is the will' (willing-heart row) and 'The heart here is the mind' (wisdom row).
fixes.fix: Delete 'not as feeling' and the three 'The heart here is the will/mind/mind and will' sentences, or replace with a text-only line, e.g. 'In these verses the heart is where a person thinks, says and decides.' State once, in the hub's lead, that the text uses the one word for all of these and the page does not sort it into mind, will and feeling.

fixes.row: What God does to the heart: gives, creates, changes, turns, opens, writes on it, humbles, makes faint; gives over
fixes.why: The label says what God does; several verses are petitions or wishes ('Turn my heart', 'Do not let my heart be drawn to evil', 'unite my heart', 'may He turn our hearts'), in which the verse does not say God did it. The note admits 'or who is asked to', but a label must say only what its verses say. The promises of Ezek 36:26 and Jer 31:33 are also future ('I will'), which the bare label hides. Exod 31:6 is skill put in craftsmen's hearts and also sits in the wisdom row.
fixes.fix: Relabel: 'What God does to the heart, or is asked to do: ...'. Add a sentence to the note that Ezek 36:26, 11:19 and Jer 31:33 are promises ('I will') made to Israel and that Heb 8:10 and 10:16 quote Jer 31:33; and that Ps 86:11, 119:36 and 141:4 are prayers.

fixes.row: Beside loving, seeking, praying, praising and giving thanks
fixes.why: These verses have the word love or thanks near the word heart, but the heart is not the one loving. Prov 19:8 in the Berean is 'He who acquires wisdom loves himself' (the Hebrew puts 'heart' as wisdom and 'loves' with the soul). Zech 8:17 is 'do not plot evil in your hearts ... and do not love to swear falsely': the loving is of oaths. Eccl 9:1 'whether love or hate' (the worker's own report calls it the weakest). Rom 1:21 is about NOT giving thanks. The row therefore says only where words are, which the project's own discipline warns against.
fixes.fix: Remove Prov 19:8, Zech 8:17, Eccl 9:1 and (or add a clause for) Rom 1:21; or make the label say 'Words of loving, seeking, praying and thanks near the word heart' and keep these, but the cleaner fix is removal. Consider also trimming the ~30 verses shared with the 'All the heart' row so the two rows do not show the same verse set.

fixes.row: Jesus knows their hearts: “I am the One who searches minds and hearts”
fixes.why: In Rev 2:23 the Greek is 'kidneys and hearts' (νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας); the Berean prints 'minds'. The row 1 note takes care to say the same of Ps 7:9 and Jer 11:20 (kidneys and heart, two words), but this row quotes 'minds and hearts' with no word on it, so it is the one place the page leaves a different word unmarked. It also hides the plainest arc in the hub: Rev 2:23 takes up the words of Jer 17:10 and Ps 7:9, 'I, the LORD, search the heart; I examine the mind (kidneys)', and speaks them in the first person of the one who speaks in Rev 2:18. Rows 1 and 2 are kept apart by hand for the divine persons, which is right, but nothing now tells the reader they say the same words.
fixes.fix: Add to the Rev 2:23 note: 'The Greek is “kidneys and hearts”, the Berean “minds and hearts”; the same two words as Ps 7:9 and Jer 11:20, and the same wording as Jer 17:10. The page does not make kidneys and heart one word.' Add νεφρός to 'Other words translated heart'. Add one cross-pointer in each of rows 1 and 2 to the other (no verdict on who is who).

fixes.why: Passages that are one speech or one pair are cut across rows with no pointer. Jer 17:9 (deceitful heart, 'Who can understand it?') is answered at once by 17:10 ('I, the LORD, search the heart'), which sits in row 1. Gen 6:5 (the heart of man evil all the time) and 6:6 (He was grieved in His heart) are consecutive verses, one in the evil row, one in the heart-of-God row. Jer 17:1 (sin engraved on the tablet of their heart) and Jer 31:33 (the law inscribed on their hearts) are the text's own pair. Circumcision of the heart runs through four rows (hardened/uncircumcised, what a person does, what God does, believers' hearts via Rom 2:29) with no single thread.
fixes.fix: Add one 'see also' sentence in each row's note, in the text's words, no verdict: Jer 17:9 with 17:10; Gen 6:5 with 6:6; Jer 17:1 with 31:33; and a line in the circumcision-bearing rows listing Lev 26:41, Deut 10:16, 30:6, Jer 4:4, 9:26, Ezek 44:7, Acts 7:51, Rom 2:29 as one thread.

fixes.row: Wisdom, understanding, sense, knowledge: a wise or discerning heart; the heart that does not understand
fixes.why: The note says the craftsmen's wisdom 'is not the wisdom of Proverbs 8'. That is a page verdict about how two texts relate; some traditions read Prov 8 and other wisdom texts together, and the text itself does not say it either way. The craftsmen are said to be 'wise of heart' and, in Exod 31:3, filled with God's Spirit in wisdom; the page should only say what the verses say.
fixes.fix: Delete 'it is not the wisdom of Proverbs 8'. Keep 'skill the text says is given to the craftsmen'; optionally add 'the wisdom hub treats Prov 8 on its own'.

fixes.row: Troubled, broken, faint or afraid; and strengthened, comforted, spoken to kindly, steady
fixes.why: Luke 24:32 ('Were not our hearts burning within us'), Acts 2:37 and 7:54 ('cut to the heart') and Luke 21:34 ('hearts weighed down') are none of: troubled, broken, faint, afraid, strengthened, comforted, steady. The row is also 115 verses with two opposites and several idioms in one label, so its label no longer predicts what a reader will find.
fixes.fix: Add 'cut to the heart, burning, weighed down' to the label, or split off a short row 'Struck and stirred: cut to the heart, burning within'. Leave the speaking-to-the-heart idiom where it is.

fixes.why: Several 'other words' show examples in which the Berean prints no 'heart' at all (qerev: Ps 5:9 'destruction lies within them', Ps 55:15; beten: Job 32:19 'my belly', Prov 22:18 'within you'), so the reader cannot see why they sit under 'translated heart'. And the Aramaic לֵב of Dan 7:28 is called 'the same word in meaning' yet shown among the different words, and is in no row: a verse for which the Berean prints 'I kept the matter to myself' and which shows neither a label nor a place.
fixes.fix: Drop the 'others' whose examples do not print heart (qerev, beten) or give each a note saying what the Berean prints and why it is listed. Fix the key so Dan 7:28 (h3821) is a row-15 verse (kept the matter in the heart) rather than an 'other word'; until the builder allows it, re-word the note so it does not claim 'the same word' while filing it under different words.

fixes.row: The body: pierced, struck, over the heart
fixes.why: 'I was asleep, but my heart was awake' (Song 5:2) is not a heart pierced, struck or worn on the chest; the other examples (2 Sam 18:14, Exod 28:29, Song 8:6, 1 Sam 25:37) are literal.
fixes.fix: Move Song 5:2 to the thinks/perceives row or 'Every other use'.

fixes.row: Beside the mouth, lips, tongue, eyes and ears
fixes.why: This row and 'Beside loving, seeking, praying...' are the two pure co-occurrence rows (89 and 77 verses). The eyes-and-ears verses (Isa 6:10, Deut 29:4, Jer 5:21) tell the story of the people who do not understand, and are the same verses as in the wisdom row and the hardened row; the mouth-and-lips verses are a different thing (heart against speech: Isa 29:13, Matt 15:8, Luke 6:45). One label covers two ideas.
fixes.fix: Either keep but relabel to say what the verses say ('The heart against the mouth, lips and tongue; the eyes and ears of the heart'), or split the eyes/ears verses to join the 'does not understand' strand. Keep the verses in every row they fit as now.

worker_points.point: 1. Total depravity / prevenient grace: five rows, one no-side sentence each, alphabetical order of labels
worker_points.why: Every claim is in the text's words, the opposite pairs (Ezek 18:31 / 36:26; Pharaoh hardens / the LORD hardens) are both shown, Rom 9:18 is left out because it has no word for heart and the note says so, and the alphabetical order is stated. A small change: the note's 'the rows below' and 'the row above' assume a fixed page order, and the alphabetical block places Evil first and What God does last, which a reader may take as a story of fall then rescue; say once that the order is by label and is not a sequence.

worker_points.point: 2. The three searcher rows (divine persons by hand)
worker_points.why: Kept by hand and no inference, which is right. Fix only: 1 John 3:20 (God greater than our hearts, knows all things) belongs in row 1, not in the believers' row; and the Rev 2:23 note should say the Greek is 'kidneys and hearts' and takes up Jer 17:10 (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 3. Row 17, the heart of God, and of Jesus
worker_points.why: Uses only the text's words and does not say how literal they are. Gen 6:5-6 is the pair that gives the row its force and should be pointed to from row 4. The row's heading carries Jesus although only Matt 11:29 speaks of His heart; the other 24 are the Hebrew Scriptures' own words about the LORD, heard first, so no OT framing problem.

The Hebrew rule is the same as the forgiveness hub's and the note lists them, so the placement is defensible. But the label is too strong for the petitions among them; add 'or is asked to' to the label rather than moving them to row 3 (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 5. Heart as mind and will, not only feeling
worker_points.why: 'Not as feeling' contradicts the glad, broken and afraid rows, and splitting the heart into mind, will and feeling is not the text's; remove (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 6. Human skill: wise of heart craftsmen in the wisdom row
worker_points.why: Keeping them with a note is right (they are 'wise of heart'). Drop only the sentence that denies a link to Prov 8; the text does not say that.

worker_points.point: 7. Hard verses kept (Heb 3:12, Isa 6:10, Isa 63:17, Rom 1:24, Rev 17:17, Ps 105:25, Prov 22:15, Ps 73:13, John 13:2, Acts 5:3)
worker_points.why: Each is shown in the row where its words put it and none is softened. Acts 5:3 / John 13:2 ('Satan filled your heart' / 'put it into the heart') are in the evil row as the verses say.

worker_points.point: Could not express: Dan 7:28 Aramaic key collision
worker_points.why: A verse with the word for heart, once, ends in no row and under 'different words' with a note that says it is the same word; fix the key rather than ship the contradiction.

worker_points.point: Row count 24; the worker suggests 9 into 7 and 16 into 15
worker_points.why: Do not merge: 16 (desire, loyalty) is not thinking; 9 is the giving and resolving heart, not what a person is told to do. 24 is inside the brief's range. The real overlaps are rows 11 and 12 (about 30 shared verses) and the two 'Beside' rows; trim rather than merge.

missing.what: Greek νεφρός (kidneys) in Rev 2:23, to sit with Hebrew כִּלְיָה under 'Other words translated heart', so the page marks the one place where 'minds' is not the heart's word in the New Testament.
The Aramaic heart in Dan 7:28 as a verse of the rows (it is the same word as the Hebrew heart, 'kept the matter in my heart'), now in no row.
A pointer in the text's own words between verses of one passage that the rows now keep apart: Jer 17:9 with 17:10 and 17:1 with 31:33; Gen 6:5 with 6:6; and the circumcision-of-the-heart thread.

examples_checked: 22 of 24 rows' examples show their label in the Berean; row 24 ('Every other use') shows no word 'heart' in 3 of its 4 examples by design, and the 'Other words' examples for qerev and beten show no 'heart' (flagged above)
summary: The hub is faithful to the text and handles the contested rows well: both sides of each pair are shown, the divine persons are by hand, and the Berean's 'minds' and 'opinions' are marked. It needs fixes to a few rows that say more than their verses do (Job 41:24 and 1 John 3:19-21 filed under the wrong labels, the prayers under 'What God does', the loosely-paired 'loving' verses), an end to the 'not as feeling' claim, and cross-pointers so passages the rows separate (Jer 17:9-10, Gen 6:5-6, Rev 2:23 and Jer 17:10) are not cut apart.
